source_text:
Ἣν εἶδον, ἀδελφοί, μετὰ ἡμέρας εἴκοσι τῆς προτέρας ὁράσεως τῆς γενομένης, εἰς τύπον τῆς θλίψεως τῆς ἐπερχομένης.
ὑπῆγον εἰς ἀγρὸν τῇ ὁδῷ τῇ καμπανῇ. ἀπὸ τῆς ὁδοῦ τῆς δημοσίας ἐστὶν ὡσεὶ στάδια δέκα: ῥᾳδίως δὲ ὁδεύεται ὁ τόπος.
μόνος οὖν περιπατῶν ἀξιῶ τὸν κύριον, ἵνα τὰς ἀποκαλύψεις καὶ τὰ ὁράματα, ἅ μοι ἔδειξεν διὰ τῆς ἁγίας Ἐκκλησίας αὐτοῦ, τελειώσῃ, ἵνα με ἰσχυροποιήσῃ καὶ δῷ τὴν μετάνοιαν τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ τοῖς ἐσκανδαλισμένοις, ἵνα δοξασθῇ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ τὸ μέγα καὶ ἔνδοξον, ὅτι με ἄξιον ἡγήσατο τοῦ δεῖξαί μοι τὰ θαυμάσια αὐτοῦ.
καὶ δοξάζοντός μου καὶ εὐχαριστοῦντος αὐτῷ, ὡς ἦχος φωνῆς μοι ἀπεκρίθη: Μὴ διψυχήσεις, Ἑρμᾶ. ἐν ἐμαυτῷ ἠρξάμην διαλογίζεσθαι καὶ λέγειν: Ἐγὼ τί ἔχω διψυχῆσαι, οὕτω τεθεμελιωμένος ὑπὸ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ ἰδὼν ἔνδοξα πράγματα;
καὶ προσέβην μικρόν, ἀδελφοί, καὶ ἰδού, βλέπω κονιορτὸν ὡς εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἠρξάμην λέγειν ἐν ἐμαυτῷ: Μήποτε κτήνη ἔρχονται καὶ κονιορτὸν ἐγείρουσιν; οὕτω δὲ ἦν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ ὡς ἀπὸ σταδίου.
γινομένου μείζονος καὶ μείζονος κονιορτοῦ ὑπενόησα εἶναί τι θεῖον: μικρὸν ἐξέλαμψεν ὁ ἥλιος καὶ ἰδού, βλέπω θηρίον μέγιστον ὡσεὶ κῆτός τι, καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ἀκρίδες πύριναι ἐξεπορεύοντο: ἦν δὲ τὸ θηρίον τῷ μήκει ὡσεὶ ποδῶν ρ, τὴν δὲ κεφαλὴν εἶχεν ὡσεὶ κεράμου.
καὶ ἠρξάμην κλαίειν καὶ ἐρωτᾶν τὸν κύριον, ἵνα με λυτρώσηται ἐξ αὐτοῦ: καὶ ἐπανεμνήσθην τοῦ ῥήματος οὗ ἀκηκόειν: Μὴ διψυχήσεις, Ἑρμᾶ.
ἐνδυσάμενος οὖν, ἀδελφοί, τὴν πίστιν τοῦ κυρίου καὶ μνησθεὶς ὧν ἐδίδαξέν με μεγαλείων, θαρσήσας εἰς τὸ θηρίον ἐμαυτὸν ἔδωκα. οὕτω δὲ ἤρχετο τὸ θηρίον ῥοίζῳ, ὥστε δύνασθαι αὐτὸ πόλιν λυμᾶναι.
ἔρχομαι ἐγγὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ τηλικοῦτο κῆτος ἐκτείνει ἑαυτὸ χαμαὶ καὶ οὐδὲν εἰ μὴ τὴν γλῶσσαν προέβαλλεν καὶ ὅλως οὐκ ἐκινήθη, μέχρις ὅτε παρῆλθον αὐτό:
εἶχεν δὲ τὸ θηρίον ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς χρώματα τέσσαρα: μέλαν, εἶτα πυροειδὲς καὶ αἱματῶδες, εἶτα χρυσοῦν, εἶτα λευκόν.
Μετὰ δὲ τὸ παρελθεῖν με τὸ θηρίον καὶ προελθεῖν ὡσεὶ πόδας λ, ἰδού, ὑπαντᾷ μοι παρθένος κεκοσμημένη ὡς ἐκ νυμφῶνος ἐκπορευομένη, ὅλη ἐν λευκοῖς καὶ ὑποδήμασιν λευκοῖς, κατακεκαλυμμένη ἕως τοῦ μετώπου, ἐν μίτρᾳ δὲ ἦν ἡ κατακάλυψις αὐτῆς: εἶχεν δὲ τὰς τρίχας αὐτῆς λευκάς.
ἔγνων ἐγὼ ἐκ τῶν προτέρων ὁραμάτων, ὅτι ἡ Ἐκκλησία ἐστίν, καὶ ἱλαρώτερος ἐγενόμην. ἀσπάζεταί με λέγουσα: Χαῖρε σύ, ἄνθρωπε. καὶ ἐγὼ αὐτὴν ἀντησπασάμην: Κυρία, χαῖρε.
ἀποκριθεῖσά μοι λέγει: Οὐδέν σοι ἀπήντησεν; λέγω αὐτῇ: Κυρία, τηλικοῦτο θηρίον, δυνάμενον λαοὺς διαφθεῖραι: ἀλλὰ τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῇ πολυσπλαγχνίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἐξέφυγον αὐτό.
Καλῶς ἐξέφυγες, φησίν, ὅτι τὴν μέριμνάν σου ἐπὶ τὸν θεὸν ἐπέριψας καὶ τὴν καρδίαν σου ἤνοιξας πρὸς τὸν κύριον, πιστεύσας, ὅτι δἰ οὐδενὸς δύνῃ σωθῆναι εἰ μὴ διὰ τοῦ μεγάλου καὶ ἐνδόξου ὀνόματος. διὰ τοῦτο ὁ κύριος ἀπέστειλεν τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ τὸν ἐπὶ τῶν θηρίων ὄντα, οὗ τὸ ὄνομά ἐστιν Θεγρί, καὶ ἐνέφραξεν τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ, ἵνα μή σε λυμάνῃ. μεγάλην θλῖψιν ἐκπέφευγας διὰ τὴν πίστιν σου καὶ ὅτι τηλικοῦτο θηρίον ἰδὼν οὐκ ἐδιψύχησας:
ὕπαγε οὖν καὶ ἐξήγησαι τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς τοῦ κυρίου τὰ μεγαλεῖα αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰπὲ αὐτοῖς, ὅτι τὸ θηρίον τοῦτο τύπος ἐστὶν θλίψεως τῆς μελλούσης τῆς μεγάλης: ἐὰν οὖν προετοιμάσησθε καὶ μετανοήσητε ἐξ ὅλης καρδίας ὑμῶν πρὸς τὸν κύριον, δυνήσεσθε ἐκφυγεῖν αὐτήν, ἐὰν ἡ καρδία ὑμῶν γένηται καθαρὰ καὶ ἄμωμος καὶ τὰς λοιπὰς τῆς ζωῆς ἡμέρας ὑμῶν δουλεύσητε τῷ κυρίῳ ἀμέμπτως. ἐπιρίψατε τὰς μερίμνας ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον, καὶ αὐτὸς κατορθώσει αὐτάς.
πιστεύσατε τῷ κυρίῳ, οἱ δίψυχοι, ὅτι πάντα δύναται καὶ ἀποστρέφει τὴν ὀργὴν αὐτοῦ ἀφ̓ ὑμῶν καὶ ἐξαποστέλλει μάστιγας ὑμῖν τοῖς διψύχοις. οὐαὶ τοῖς ἀκούσασιν τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα καὶ παρακούσασιν: αἱρετώτερον ἦν αὐτοῖς τὸ μὴ γεννηθῆναι.
Ἠρώτησα αὐτὴν περὶ τῶν τεσσάρων χρωμάτων ὧν εἶχεν τὸ θηρίον εἰς τὴν κεφαλήν. ἡ δὲ ἀποκριθεῖσά μοι λέγει: Πάλιν περίεργος εἶ περὶ τοιούτων πραγμάτων. Ναί, φημί, κυρία: γνώρισόν μοι, τί ἐστιν ταῦτα.
Ἄκουε, φησίν: τὸ μὲν μέλαν οὗτος ὁ κόσμος ἐστίν, ἐν ᾧ κατοικεῖτε:
τὸ δὲ πυροειδὲς καὶ αἱματῶδες, ὅτι δεῖ τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον δἰ αἵματος καὶ πυρὸς ἀπόλλυσθαι:
τὸ δὲ χρυσοῦν μέρος ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ ἐκφυγόντες τὸν κόσμον τοῦτον. ὥσπερ γὰρ τὸ χρυσίον δοκιμάζεται διὰ τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ εὔχρηστον γίνεται, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς δοκιμάζεσθε οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐν αὐτοῖς. οἱ οὖν μείναντες καὶ πυρωθέντες ὑπ’ αὐτῶν καθαρισθήσεσθε. ὥσπερ τὸ χρυσίον ἀποβάλλει τὴν σκωρίαν αὐτοῦ, οὕτω καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀποβαλεῖτε πᾶσαν λύπην καὶ στενοχωρίαν, καὶ καθαρισθήσεσθε καὶ χρήσιμοι ἔσεσθε εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν τοῦ πύργου.
τὸ δὲ λευκὸν μέρος ὁ αἰὼν ὁ ἐπερχόμενός ἐστιν, ἐν ᾧ κατοικήσουσιν οἱ ἐκλεκτοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ: ὅτι ἄσπιλοι καὶ καθαροὶ ἔσονται οἱ ἐκλελεγμένοι ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
σὺ οὖν μὴ διαλίπῃς λαλῶν εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῶν ἁγίων. ἔχετε καὶ τὸν τύπον τῆς θλίψεως τῆς ἐρχομένης μεγάλης. ἐὰν δὲ ὑμεῖς θελήσητε, οὐδὲν ἔσται. μνημονεύετε τὰ προγεγραμμένα.
ταῦτα εἴπασα ἀπῆλθεν, καὶ οὐκ εἶδον, ποίῳ τόπῳ ἀπῆλθεν: νέφος γὰρ ἐγένετο: κἀγὼ ἐπεστράφην εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω φοβηθείς, δοκῶν ὅτι τὸ θηρίον ἔρχεται.
thought_title: The Beast as a Type of the Coming Tribulation
orientation: Hermas tells his fellow believers about a vision he had on a country road outside Rome, twenty days after the last one. He meets a huge beast that stands for the coming tribulation, and then the Church, who earlier appeared as an old woman and now comes dressed as a bride.
pass_a_gloss: The vision which I saw, brothers, after twenty days of the former vision that had occurred, was for a type of the tribulation that is coming upon us. I was going into the country by the Campanian road. From the public road it is about ten stades; and the place is easily traveled. So walking alone I ask the Lord that he might complete the revelations and the visions which he showed me through his holy Church, that he might strengthen me and give repentance to his servants who have been scandalized, that his great and glorious name might be glorified, because he considered me worthy to show me his wonders. And as I was glorifying and giving thanks to him, as it were a sound of a voice answered me: Do not be double-minded, Hermas. In myself I began to reason and say: What do I have to be double-minded about, being so founded by the Lord and having seen glorious things? And I went forward a little, brothers, and behold, I see dust as if up to heaven and I began to say in myself: Are cattle perhaps coming and stirring up dust? And it was from me about a stade away. As the dust became greater and greater I suspected it was something divine: the sun shone out a little and behold, I see a beast most great, like some sea-monster, and from its mouth fiery locusts were coming forth: and the beast was in length about a hundred feet, and it had its head like a jar. And I began to weep and to ask the Lord that he might rescue me from it: and I remembered the word which I had heard: Do not be double-minded, Hermas. So having put on, brothers, the faith of the Lord and having remembered the great things which he taught me, taking courage I gave myself over to the beast. And the beast was coming with such a rushing sound that it could destroy a city. I come near to it, and the sea-monster of such size stretches itself out on the ground and nothing except the tongue did it put forth and it did not move at all, until I passed by it: and the beast had on its head four colors: black, then fire-colored and blood-colored, then golden, then white. And after I passed by the beast and went forward about thirty feet, behold, a virgin meets me adorned as if coming out of a bridal chamber, all in white garments and white sandals, veiled down to the forehead, and her covering was a headband: and she had her hair white. I knew from the former visions that it is the Church, and I became more cheerful. She greets me saying: Hail to you, man. And I greeted her in return: Lady, hail. Answering me she says: Did nothing meet you? I say to her: Lady, a sea-monster of such size, able to destroy peoples: but by the power of the Lord and by his great mercy I escaped it. You escaped well, she says, because you cast your care upon God and you opened your heart toward the Lord, believing that through no one can you be saved except through the great and glorious name. For this reason the Lord sent his angel who is over the beasts, whose name is Thegri, and he blocked its mouth, so that it might not harm you. You have escaped a great tribulation through your faith and because seeing a sea-monster of such size you did not become double-minded: go therefore and explain to the elect of the Lord his great works and tell them that this beast is a type of the tribulation that is to come, the great one: if therefore you prepare yourselves and repent from your whole heart toward the Lord, you will be able to escape it, if your heart becomes pure and blameless and for the remaining days of your life you serve the Lord blamelessly. Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he will set them right. Believe in the Lord, you double-minded ones, that he can do all things and turns away his anger from you and sends out scourges upon you, the double-minded. Woe to those who hear these words and disobey them: it would have been better for them not to have been born. I asked her about the four colors which the beast had on its head. And she answering me says: Again you are overly curious about such things. Yes, I say, lady: make known to me what these are. Listen, she says: the black is this world, in which you dwell: and the fire-colored and blood-colored, that this world must be destroyed through blood and fire: and the golden part is you who have escaped this world. For just as gold is tested through fire and becomes useful, so also you are tested who dwell in them. So those who remain and are burned by them will be purified. Just as gold casts off its dross, so also you will cast off all grief and distress, and you will be purified and will be useful for the building of the tower. And the white part is the age that is coming, in which the elect of God will dwell: because spotless and pure will be those chosen by God for eternal life. So do not cease speaking into the ears of the saints. You have also the type of the tribulation that is coming, the great one. But if you are willing, it will be nothing. Remember the things written beforehand. Having said these things she departed, and I did not see to what place she departed: for a cloud came to be: and I turned back behind me in fear, thinking that the beast is coming.

choices.why: The adjective καμπανῇ is a proper adjective referring to the Campanian region; rendering as a proper name preserves the geographical specificity.
κῆτος denotes a large sea creature; 'sea-monster' conveys the monstrous size and marine nature without modern 'whale' connotations.

choices.english: having put on the faith of the Lord
choices.why: The metaphor of putting on faith as a garment is preserved literally; 'put on' keeps the clothing imagery.
rejected: having clothed myself with the faith of the Lord
having taken up the faith of the Lord

choices.why: ῥοῖζος denotes a rushing, whizzing, or roaring noise; 'rushing sound' captures the onomatopoeic force.

choices.english: adorned as if coming out of a bridal chamber
choices.why: The simile is kept literal; 'bridal chamber' renders νυμφών precisely, and the participle preserves the sense of emerging.
rejected: adorned like a bride coming out

choices.why: περίεργος means meddlesome or overly inquisitive about matters beyond one's concern; 'overly curious' captures the mild rebuke.

pass_b_english: Brothers, this is the vision I saw twenty days after the earlier vision had come to me. It was a foreshadowing of the tribulation that is coming.
I was going out to the country along the Campanian road. The place is about ten furlongs from the public road, and it is easy going.

As I walked alone, I asked the Lord to complete the revelations and the visions he had shown me through his holy Church. I asked that he would make me strong and give repentance to his servants who had stumbled. I asked this so that his great and glorious name might be glorified, because he had counted me worthy to be shown his wonders.

While I was glorifying him and giving him thanks, something like the sound of a voice answered me, “Do not be double-minded, Hermas.” I began to turn this over within myself. I said, “Why should I be double-minded, when the Lord has set me on so firm a foundation and I have seen glorious things?”

I went on a little farther, brothers, and look, I saw a cloud of dust that seemed to reach the sky. I began to say to myself, “Could that be cattle coming, and raising the dust?” It was about a furlong away from me.

The cloud of dust grew greater and greater, and I suspected that it was something divine. The sun shone out a little, and look, I saw an enormous beast, like some sea monster, and fiery locusts were coming out of its mouth. The beast was about a hundred feet long, and its head looked like earthenware.
I began to weep, and to beg the Lord to rescue me from it. Then I remembered the word I had heard: “Do not be double-minded, Hermas.”

So, brothers, I put on the faith of the Lord and called to mind the great things he had taught me. I took courage and went to face the beast. And the beast came rushing on with such a noise that it could have laid a city waste.
I came close to it, and that huge sea monster stretched itself out on the ground. It did nothing but put out its tongue, and it did not stir at all until I had passed it by.
The beast had four colors on its head: black, then the color of fire and blood, then gold, then white.

After I had passed the beast and gone on about thirty feet, look, a virgin came to meet me. She was adorned as though she were coming out of a bridal chamber, all in white and with white sandals. She was veiled as far as the forehead, with a headdress for her covering, and her hair was white.
From the earlier visions I knew that she was the Church, and I grew more cheerful. She greeted me and said, “Greetings to you, man.” I greeted her in return: “Lady, greetings.”
She answered me, “Did nothing meet you?” I said to her, “Lady, a beast so huge that it could destroy whole peoples. But by the power of the Lord and by his great compassion I escaped it.”

“You did well to escape it,” she said, “because you cast your care upon God and opened your heart to the Lord. You believed that you can be saved by nothing except the great and glorious name. For this reason the Lord sent his angel, the one who is over the beasts, whose name is Thegri, and shut the beast’s mouth so that it would do you no harm. You have escaped a great tribulation because of your faith, and because you saw so huge a beast and were not double-minded.

“Go, then, and tell the Lord’s elect of his mighty works. Tell them that this beast is a foreshadowing of the great tribulation that is to come. If, then, you prepare yourselves ahead of time and repent to the Lord with your whole heart, you will be able to escape it. You will be able to, if your heart becomes pure and unblemished and you serve the Lord blamelessly for the rest of the days of your life. Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he will set them right.

“Believe the Lord, you double-minded: he can do all things. He turns his wrath away from you, and he sends scourges upon you who are double-minded. Woe to those who hear these words and refuse to heed them. It would have been better for them not to have been born.”
I asked her about the four colors that the beast had on its head. She answered me, “Again you are too curious about such things.” “Yes, lady,” I said. “Make known to me what they are.”
“Listen,” she said. “The black is this world in which you live.
“The color of fire and blood means that this world must perish by blood and fire.

“The golden part is you, who have fled from this world. For just as gold is tested by fire and becomes useful, so you also are being tested, you who live among them. Those of you who endure, and are put through the fire by them, will be made pure. Just as gold casts off its dross, so you too will cast off all grief and anguish. You will be made pure, and you will be useful for the building of the tower.
“The white part is the age to come, in which the elect of God will live. For those whom God has chosen for eternal life will be spotless and pure.

“So you must not stop speaking in the hearing of the saints. All of you have this too: the foreshadowing of the great tribulation that is coming. But if you are willing, it will be nothing. Remember what was written before.”
When she had said these things she went away, and I did not see where she went, for a cloud came. And I turned around in fear, thinking that the beast was coming.

problems.why: Same group referred to with slight variations that may confuse
Noun, adjective, and verb forms used for same concept; reader may miss connection

problems.quote: Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he will set them right (1 Peter 5:7)
problems.why: Cited as 1 Peter 5:7 but text says 'set them right'; actual verse says 'he cares for you'
problems.fix: Note: citation approximate; text adapts the verse

problems.quote: it would have been better for them not to have been born (Matthew 26:24)
problems.why: Cited as Matthew 26:24 but actual verse refers to Judas specifically; here applied generally
problems.fix: Note: application is extended beyond original context

problems.quote: Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he will set them right (1 Peter 5:7).
problems.why: The reference is correct but the wording 'set them right' differs from standard 'casting all your anxieties on him'.
problems.fix: Align with standard translation or note it is a paraphrase.

problems.quote: it would have been better for them not to have been born (Matthew 26:24).
problems.why: Matthew 26:24 says 'better for that man if he had not been born'; the plural 'them' does not match.
problems.fix: Note the adaptation from singular to plural, or cite the general tradition.

edits.old: Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he will set them right (1 Peter 5:7).
edits.new: Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he will set them right (cf. 1 Peter 5:7).

edits.old: it would have been better for them not to have been born (Matthew 26:24).
edits.new: it would have been better for them not to have been born (cf. Matthew 26:24).

fixed: The glossary problems about 'the elect' and 'double-mindedness' are not translation errors; the English already uses the glossary terms consistently ('the elect', 'double-minded', 'double-mindedness'), so no edit is needed.
The scripture citation for 1 Peter 5:7 is a paraphrase ('set them right' vs. 'he cares for you'), so I added 'cf.' to mark it as an allusion rather than a direct quotation.
The scripture citation for Matthew 26:24 is applied generally to a plural group rather than to Judas specifically, so I added 'cf.' to mark it as an allusion rather than a direct quotation.

problems.why: Inconsistent capitalization makes it unclear when 'church' is the allegorical woman/institution vs. generic.
problems.fix: Capitalize consistently when referring to the allegorical Church.

problems.why: These terms overlap but are not identical; reader cannot tell if 'elect' = 'saints' or if distinctions exist.
problems.fix: Add note that 'elect' and 'saints' are largely synonymous in this text.

problems.quote: a type of the tribulation that is coming
problems.why: 'Type' is technical theological term (typos) unexplained; modern reader thinks 'kind/sort'.

problems.quote: Remember what has been written before.
problems.why: Vague reference; possibly to earlier part of Shepherd itself, not OT Scripture.
problems.fix: Clarify this refers to earlier revelations in the book, not biblical text.

edits.old: a type of the tribulation that is coming
edits.new: a prophetic symbol of the tribulation that is coming

edits.old: Remember what has been written before.
edits.new: Remember the things written earlier in this book.

fixed: Capitalization of 'church': The English already capitalizes 'Church' when referring to the allegorical woman ('through his holy Church', 'she was the Church'), so no edit is needed.

Elect/saints overlap: The source uses 'τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς τοῦ κυρίου' (the elect of the Lord) and 'τῶν ἁγίων' (the saints) in the same passage; they are largely synonymous, but the English preserves both terms, so no edit is needed.
Type: The source uses 'τύπος' (type), which is a technical term; the English 'type' is accurate but unclear to modern readers, so I changed it to 'prophetic symbol'.

Remember what has been written before: The source 'τὰ προγεγραμμένα' refers to things written earlier in the Shepherd itself, not Scripture, so I clarified it as 'the things written earlier in this book'.

polish.changed: Clarified speaker transitions, replaced 'sea-monster' with 'sea creature' for modern readers, removed scripture cross-references that were not in the source, and smoothed sentence flow while preserving every claim and detail.

notes.why: Same group referred to with slight variations; 'elect' alone may seem different from 'elect of God'.
notes.fix: Consistently use 'elect' or add explanatory note.
Add note: about 1.2 miles or 2 km.

notes.why: Same issue; singular form of stades.
notes.fix: Add note: about 600 feet or 185 meters.

notes.why: Name of angel over beasts with no explanation or context.
notes.fix: Add note: Thegri is an angelic name from Jewish apocalyptic tradition.

notes.why: Modern reader thinks of mythical beast; Greek 'ketos' could be whale or large sea creature.
notes.fix: Use 'great sea creature' or note 'sea-monster' is literal translation.

notes.quote: Cast your cares upon the Lord, and he will set them right (cf. 1 Peter 5:7).
notes.why: The allusion is to Psalm 55:22 (LXX) or 1 Peter 5:7; but the text says 'as it is written' earlier for Eldad and Modat, not for this.
notes.fix: Check: the citation format is correct as 'cf.', not claiming direct quote.

notes.quote: Woe to those who hear these words and disobey them; it would have been better for them not to have been born (cf. Matthew 26:24).
notes.why: Matthew 26:24 refers to Judas; the woe formula is more general in Mark 14:21.
notes.fix: Note: the 'better not born' formula applies to Judas specifically in Matthew, used more generally here.

notes.why: Thegri is an unexplained angelic name; the reader has no context for it.
notes.fix: Add a note: 'Thegri: an angelic name otherwise unattested; possibly a variant of a known angel name in apocryphal tradition.'

notes.quote: I was going out to the country by the Campanian road
notes.why: The Campanian road is a specific Roman road, but no map or context is provided.
